articles.title: Coinbase Tokenized Stocks Live on Base
articles.summary: Coinbase launched four tokenized equities on Base under the B20 standard (NVDAc, METAc, AAPLc, and GOOGLc), with shares held 1:1 by Alpaca under Abu Dhabi Global Market supervision, restricted to non-US users in eligible jurisdictions. Day-one activity reached $4.55M in combined onchain value, $3.06M in DEX liquidity, and $10.8M in 24-hour volume across approximately 50 integrated protocols including Aave, Morpho, Aerodrome, 0x, and 1inch. B20 extends ERC-20 for full composability with existing wallets and routers. Dividends and splits settle via an onchain multiplier that keeps position balances static, preventing disruptions to DeFi collateral positions. The launch enters a $2.48B tokenized public equities market currently led by Ondo at $872.7M, with agentic trading integrations already underway through Virtuals and Treasures.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Crypto's Next Billion Users, Paying With Stablecoins
articles.summary: AI agents are emerging as a distinct crypto user cohort, autonomously spending stablecoins to pay for services without human approval loops. Coinbase's head of AI product characterizes the current moment as the "Napster/LimeWire era" of agentic payments, placing the category at an early, pre-mainstream inflection point where infrastructure and norms are still forming. Coinbase is building at the AI/crypto payments intersection, targeting a wave of machine-initiated transactions that operate outside traditional user onboarding funnels. The protocols and rails that capture agent wallet share now could define the settlement layer for machine commerce at scale, making stablecoin-denominated micropayments a structural demand driver rather than a cyclical one.

articles.title: EntropyIO: First Liquid Markets for Private Company Exposure
articles.summary: EntropyIO has launched liquid perpetual markets for private company exposure on Hyperliquid, with Anthropic as its first underlying asset. Most AI value accrues in private companies accessible only via VC rounds or secondary markets with high minimums, and EntropyIO targets that gap by routing demand through Hyperliquid's permissionless order book. The launch marks the first onchain venue for continuous price discovery on a private company of Anthropic's scale. It will compete with trade[xyz] for Hyperliquid-based equity perpetuals and related assets.

articles.title: Elysium: A New Era for Hyperliquid
articles.summary: Kinetiq, which holds the majority of HyperEVM TVL and economic activity, is launching Elysium, an L2 built to resolve HyperEVM's throughput constraints and swap costs that reach $20 per transaction. Elysium adopts HYPE as its gas token instead of USDC, targets block time parity with HyperCore, and ships an L1Read precompile that grants PropAMMs top-of-block oracle freshness, enabling tighter quotes than HyperEVM's architecture permits. A native token generation platform creates an unbroken path from long-tail AMM bootstrapping through Elysium PropAMM integration, HyperCore spot orderbook listing, and eventual HIP-3 perpetual listing, all within one ecosystem. Sequencer fees split 50% toward programmatic open-market KNTQ purchases burned in full to the Hyperliquid Assistance Fund, with the remaining 50% split equally between builders and the Kinetiq treasury.

articles.title: Building Risk-Aware AI Agents for Vault Curation
articles.summary: Gauntlet's Aria agent operates within a staged autonomy model (tool to scoped delegate to orchestrator), with all production vault changes requiring one or two human approvals before execution. In production, Aria has triaged 450+ risk alerts and reviewed 200+ pull requests, with 61 merged post-human approval. The core architectural principle separates offchain reasoning (unconstrained access to live data and compute) from onchain authority enforced via Aera's merkle-root committed guardian permissions, making delegation cryptographically precise and auditable. Gauntlet built its own agentic harness rather than using commercial platforms, citing ownership of controls and action verifiability as non-outsourceable requirements for adversarial DeFi environments.

articles.title: Where Should Your Stablecoins Go to Earn?
articles.summary: Kamino, Jupiter Lend, and Loopscale control roughly 92% of Solana's tracked stablecoin lending TVL, each built on a distinct architecture. Kamino's shared pool isolates riskier collateral in separate markets, backed by 15 audits, 4 formal verifications, and no confirmed exploits since its 2023 launch. Jupiter Lend routes both depositor capital and leveraged borrowing through a single Liquidity Layer, with dynamic withdrawal ceilings throttling liquidity-shock risk. Loopscale's Credit Order Book pairs lenders and borrowers at fixed rates and durations, offering rate certainty over pool depth, though it carries the only confirmed exploit among the three: a $5.8M price feed attack in April 2025 where all funds were recovered within 48 hours via a negotiated 10% bounty. The choice maps to variable-rate liquidity depth (Kamino), combined earn-and-borrow exposure with shock controls (Jupiter), and predictable fixed rates with thinner markets (Loopscale).

articles.title: Non-custodial crypto card providers that aren't really non-custodial
articles.summary: Neobanks that force users to delete their account to export private keys are contradicting crypto's not your keys, not your crypto ethos while claiming non-custody's compliance benefits. The underlying double-spend risk (card swipe plus simultaneous onchain drain) is solvable via smart contract wallets and account abstraction.

articles.title: Comparing tokenized-stock structures across major exchanges
articles.summary: This post breaks down how Coinbase, Binance, Kraken, Robinhood, and Backpack structure tokenized equities differently around redemption control, trading venue, and dividend handling. Ondo still holds ~70% of the tokenized-stock market, but competition from major exchanges launching their own wrappers is intensifying.

articles.title: EUR-to-USD conversion fees on Plasma One
articles.summary: A €10 Wise deposit converted to $11.64 on Plasma One versus a Google-quoted $11.66 and Wise-quoted $11.67, implying roughly a 0.2-0.3% conversion spread.

articles.title: Fasset's gold-backed neobank card with Tether
articles.summary: Fasset, an Islamic crypto neobank that just raised at a $1B valuation, partnered with Tether on a gold-backed card paying up to 6% cashback in XAUt.

articles.title: Cosmos EVM Security Incident Forces Chain Halts
articles.summary: A security incident in the Cosmos EVM module prompted Cosmos Labs to advise validators across affected chains to halt operations while its engineering team investigates.

articles.title: Comparing Base tokenized stock pricing to traditional brokers
articles.summary: Testing Base stock quotes via Aerodrome against Interactive Brokers found Base pricing about 32 cents cheaper than IBKR's tiered plan and 97 cents cheaper than IBKR's fixed plan (measured at market close, pending an open-market re-quote).
